basics.name: Jesús Daniel Medina Cruz
basics.label: Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) Expert | Senior Mobile Software Engineer
basics.summary: Senior Mobile Engineer with 11 years of experience architecting scalable Android and cross-platform systems. Specialized in Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) to maximize code sharing across Android, iOS, and Desktop environments without sacrificing native performance. Proven track record of leading migrations, modernizing legacy systems, and establishing robust CI/CD pipelines to accelerate delivery cycles in fast-paced startup and enterprise environments.

work.name: Wells Fargo
work.summary: Led the modernization and architectural redesign of critical navigation flows for one of the largest banking applications in the US, serving tens of millions of customers.
highlights: Architected a centralized, 100% testable navigation system consolidating 10+ fragmented entry points, significantly reducing technical debt and eliminating duplicate logic.
Led the strategic UI modernization initiative, spearheading the migration of legacy XML layouts to Jetpack Compose while enforcing Clean Architecture and MVVM patterns.
Increased test coverage and stability across the app by moving navigation logic out of Fragments into isolated, testable domain layers.
Mentored the engineering team on modern Android practices (Compose, Kotlin/Native, MVVM) and integrated AI tools (GitHub Copilot, Devin) to accelerate development velocity.

work.name: Academia Desde0
work.summary: Directed curriculum development at a training platform founded to democratize access to high-quality tech education for Spanish-speaking communities.
highlights: Upskilled developers in modern mobile architecture by designing and delivering a curriculum focused on KMP and modern architectural patterns.
Improved code quality and team collaboration by establishing pair programming, structured code reviews, and agile feedback cycles.
Runs a catalog of in-person and live online courses for non-programmers and experienced professionals; student-born projects include Bubble, Zora, Gobus, and Maxiser.

work.summary: Series A audio content startup backed by Greylock & Accel (5M+ downloads); entire original audio content catalog acquired by Spotify. Hired to move the React Native app to fully native Android and iOS.
work.name: Beek.io
highlights: Owned the native Android and iOS apps end to end during the migration from React Native to fully native clients.
Built a complete audio player in Kotlin Multiplatform with native Jetpack Compose and SwiftUI interfaces, covering background playback, offline-first synchronization, and lock-screen controls.
Architected multiplatform shared libraries using Kotlin Multiplatform, eliminating code duplication between Android and iOS for network layer, models, and analytics.
Spearheaded Android codebase modernization, migrating legacy monolithic architectures into modular Kotlin packages and reducing technical debt by 31%.
Introduced CI/CD from scratch with CircleCI and Fastlane, replacing manual releases with automated debug and release builds and internal testing distribution on Google Play and the App Store.
Engineered smooth in-app purchasing (IAP) funnels and audio catalog discovery, increasing subscription conversion and playback session length.
Modified REST and GraphQL endpoints in Ruby on Rails to unblock mobile features.
Maintained 99.9% crash-free sessions across high-frequency audio streaming and dynamic catalog search.

work.name: Bitso
highlights: Owned the integration of the CleverTap user engagement SDK through Kotlin Multiplatform, sharing a single implementation across the Android and iOS apps.

work.summary: Early-stage startup building a short-video social app with crypto features.
work.name: Vlokr (early-stage startup)
highlights: Joined as the first engineering hire, working directly with the CTO; selected the full technology stack and planned, designed, and built the Android app in native Kotlin.
Built the serverless AWS backend, with S3 video uploads and an AWS-managed database.
Delivered a working MVP with video playback, thumbnails, comments, and likes.

work.summary: Mobile SDKs behind Dexcom's continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) apps.
work.name: Dexcom
highlights: Wrote unit and integration tests with JUnit 4 and JUnit 5 for the Kotlin and Java SDKs used by the G6 and G7 CGM mobile apps.
Championed robust testing practices and SDK development for high-trust health apps.

work.name: Insulet Corporation
work.summary: Spearheaded the development of the VIEW app, an innovative mobile solution empowering caregivers to remotely monitor the health of individuals living with diabetes.
highlights: Migrated the VIEW codebase from Java to Kotlin and introduced the app's first Kotlin Multiplatform module, which powers the CGM graph.
Designed the app's offline-first architecture with local Room/SQLite persistence.
Delivered continuous health monitoring by designing a high-concurrency client data processing pipeline with low-latency background updates.
Reduced app memory footprint by 35% and eliminated UI stutter by isolating background telemetry processing into dedicated memory-optimized domain layers.

work.name: arkusnexus
work.summary: Built mobile features for Rosy, a memory assistant running on custom embedded hardware, and Simplicity, an insurtech telematics app.
highlights: Built the text-to-speech system for the Rosy memory assistant as a native Android module inside a React Native app running on custom embedded hardware.
Engineered real-time vehicle telematics and sensor tracking over Bluetooth for Simplicity's dynamic insurtech pricing models.

work.name: Compus Sistemas Express
work.summary: Rebuilt legacy Visual FoxPro business systems as native Android apps, written from scratch in Java.
highlights: Built multiple Android apps from scratch in Java to replace Visual FoxPro systems: salvage-vehicle buying and selling, shipping, and materials check-in and check-out.
Built Auto Parts, an auto parts sales platform for Android.
Boosted development velocity for internal projects by creating reusable SDKs and service clients to standardize data access.
